title: AI-Generated Rubric Interfaces: K–12 Teachers’ Perceptions and Practices
extended_summary:
This paper examines how K–12 teachers perceive and use AI-supported rubric generation for assessment and feedback, with a focus on whether such tools can reduce the burden of creating rubrics while still preserving teacher control and instructional alignment. The authors specifically ask how teachers view large language models for generating rubrics and assessments in block-based programming contexts, and whether hands-on exposure changes their willingness to adopt these tools in practice.

The intervention studied was a summer professional development workshop in which 25 middle- and high-school teachers used MagicSchool.ai to generate rubrics, practiced prompting to tailor criteria and performance levels, and then used the AI-generated rubrics to assess a sample block-based programming task. Teachers also used the platform’s chatbot, Reina, to generate rubric-based feedback for the same work. Data came from pre- and post-workshop surveys, open-ended reflections, discussions, and exit tickets, and the qualitative component was analyzed thematically.

Across both survey and qualitative findings, teachers viewed AI-generated rubrics as useful starting drafts that improved structure, clarity, and speed, especially for vague or creative tasks. However, they repeatedly emphasized that the outputs often required substantial editing, sometimes used generic or grade-misaligned language, and could miss instructional priorities. Teachers were generally positive about clarity, transparency, and ethical acceptability, but less satisfied with usability, especially the ability to add, remove, or revise criteria. Overall, the study concludes that AI rubric tools are most promising when they are teacher-directed, editable, standards- and goal-aligned, and supported by scaffolded prompting rather than presented as fixed automated products.

identified_tools.name: MagicSchool.ai
identified_tools.description: An AI-enabled educational platform that can generate and help refine teacher-authored classroom materials such as rubrics and feedback via prompting and chat-based interaction.
identified_tools.use_case: Teachers used MagicSchool.ai to generate AI rubrics for a block-based programming task, practiced prompting to tailor criteria and performance levels, and then used the generated rubrics to assess a sample assignment; they also used the platform's chatbot (Reina) to produce rubric-based feedback.

findings.finding_summary: Teachers reported that MagicSchool.ai-generated rubrics were useful as strong starting drafts that reduced the time and effort of creating rubrics from scratch. The tool was seen as improving structure and clarifying vague criteria, but many teachers said outputs still required substantial editing and teacher oversight.
findings.measure: Teacher perceptions of rubric generation usefulness, workload reduction, and editability from surveys, open-ended responses, and thematic analysis

findings.finding_summary: Teachers rated the generated rubrics positively for criteria clarity (M=3.9375), performance-level differentiation (M=4.125), assignment alignment (M=4.0), and transparency (M=4.062), but were more mixed on grade-level language appropriateness (M=3.5) and curriculum/learning-outcome alignment (M=3.5). The lowest usability rating concerned adding/removing/revising criteria without difficulty (M=2.75), indicating friction in customization.
findings.measure: Post-survey Likert ratings of clarity, alignment, usability, and ethical factors

findings.finding_summary: Teachers perceived AI-generated feedback as more detailed and scalable but sometimes harsher than their own feedback, creating a strictness-versus-detail tradeoff. They emphasized that adoption should remain teacher-directed, with outputs calibrated and reviewed before use with students.
findings.measure: Open-ended reflections on feedback quality and willingness to use AI-generated feedback

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic large-language-model chatbot or generative AI system used to draft rubrics and provide rubric-based feedback when no specific model product is identified beyond the platform context.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper also refers generically to a chatbot/LLM workflow within the rubric-generation platform and to the use of a chatbot for delivering rubric-based feedback, without naming a standalone model beyond MagicSchool.ai's integrated chatbot.

findings.finding_summary: Teachers reported that the chatbot-enabled workflow could provide scalable, detailed feedback and support quicker rubric-based assessment than manual grading alone. Adoption was conditional on the system remaining configurable so teachers could retain control over criteria, weighting, and final judgments.
findings.measure: Teacher perceptions from surveys and open-ended responses about AI-assisted grading and feedback workflow

findings.finding_summary: Teachers found that prompt clarity and detail affected output quality: more descriptive prompts yielded deeper feedback, while vague prompting could produce outputs that were generic or misaligned with instructional priorities. This supports an iterative human-in-the-loop workflow rather than fixed automation.
findings.measure: Open-ended reflections on prompt quality, output depth, and alignment

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative/mixed-methods workshop study with surveys and thematic analysis, not an experimental impact study. It provides useful evidence about teacher perceptions and workflow features, but not causal effects on student outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports meaningful practitioner uptake and workflow benefits, but these are perception-based and no quantitative student-performance effect sizes are reported. Impact is promising for teacher workflow, but the educational outcome impact remains unclear.
